mainTopic: The plural ״לֹא תִשְׁחֲטוּ״, and whether סומכוס gives double punishment for one act with one warning
overview: The amud opens by defending a lesson from the plural word ״לֹא תִשְׁחֲטוּ״ in the פסוק of אותו ואת בנו. Since the תורה could have written ״לֹא תִשְׁחוֹט״ or ״לֹא יִשְׁחֲטוּ״, the chosen wording teaches two lessons at once. Next, אביי asks רב יוסף why סומכוס gives eighty lashes to one who slaughters a mother, its granddaughter, and then the daughter. רב יוסף answers that סומכוס holds a general rule: two כזיתים of חלב eaten in one העלם bring two חטאות. The גמרא tries to prove this from a ברייתא about one who sows כלאים כלאים. That proof is rejected, because the ברייתא can follow the רבנן and teach that there are two kinds of כלאים, against רבי יאשיה. A second proof comes from the משנה about eating from both גיד הנשה nerves. That proof is also rejected: the משנה can be about separate acts following the רבנן, with another tradition that רבי יהודה holds התראת ספק counts as a warning. The source for that tradition, a ברייתא about נותר of the קרבן פסח, begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Isn't this verse needed for the basic prohibition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier דרשה: the פסוק ״לֹא תִשְׁחֲטוּ״ is needed to teach the basic איסור of אותו ואת בנו, so how can it teach anything extra?
steps.simpleTranslation: This verse is needed for its own basic point.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the lesson just learned from ״לֹא תִשְׁחֲטוּ״. It argues that the פסוק is already busy teaching the main איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק that is needed for its basic law usually can't also be used for an extra דרשה. So the challenge asks: where is the 'extra' in this פסוק that lets us learn more from it?

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (a different purpose)
For itself, meaning for its own basic law
The איסור of slaughtering a mother animal and its offspring on the same day

phrases.english: Isn't this needed for itself?
phrases.notes: "For itself" means for the basic איסור of not slaughtering a mother and its child on the same day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the דרשה from ״לֹא תִשְׁחֲטוּ״ made just before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier extra lesson drawn from ״לֹא תִשְׁחֲטוּ״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is needed for the basic איסור, so there is no extra wording left over to learn from.

steps.title: The plural form is extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if the פסוק only taught the basic איסור, it would have said ״לֹא תִשְׁחוֹט״ in the singular. The plural ״לֹא תִשְׁחֲטוּ״ is extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the תורה write "you [singular] shall not slaughter." Why does it say "you [plural] shall not slaughter"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The basic law would only need the singular word, so the plural form shows there is an extra lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not deny that the פסוק teaches the basic איסור. It points to the specific plural ending as the extra part. That extra wording is what the דרשה is built on.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let [the תורה] write
You (singular) shall not slaughter
You (plural) shall not slaughter, the actual wording of the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: Both ״תִשְׁחוֹט״ and ״תִשְׁחֲטוּ״ mean "slaughter." The whole argument depends on the difference between the singular and the plural endings, so watch the last letters.

phrases.english: If so, let it write "you shall not slaughter" (singular),
Why does it say "you shall not slaughter" (plural)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to extra wording in the פסוק (plural instead of singular)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole פסוק is used up by the basic איסור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The plural ending is extra, so it can teach an additional lesson.

steps.title: The plural is needed to include two people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: the plural is still needed, to teach that the איסור applies even when two different people do the two slaughterings.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is still needed. If the תורה had written the singular, I would have said one person, yes, but two people, no. So the תורה wrote the plural to include even two people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back again. It says the plural has its own job: to teach that two separate people are also included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a singular word, one might think the איסור applies only when the same person slaughters both animals. The plural would then be used up teaching that two people are also included. If so, it is not free for the earlier lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: But still / nevertheless
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
I would have thought, a mistaken first assumption
One [person]... two [people]

phrases.english: But it is still needed,
for if the Merciful One had written "you shall not slaughter" (singular),

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: חַד – אִין, תְּרֵי – לָא.
phrases.english: I would have said: one person, yes; two people, no.
phrases.notes: He means it would be forbidden only if the same person slaughtered both the mother and its child.

phrases.english: So the Merciful One wrote "you shall not slaughter" (plural), to include even two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the plural ending is extra
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plural is needed to include two separate slaughterers, so it is not extra.

steps.title: "They shall not be slaughtered" would have covered two people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that to include two people, the תורה could have written ״לֹא יִשְׁחֲטוּ״ ("they shall not be slaughtered"). Choosing ״לֹא תִשְׁחֲטוּ״ shows something more.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let it write "they shall not be slaughtered." Why does it say "you [plural] shall not slaughter"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge. A different wording would have covered two people, so the actual wording must be teaching an additional lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״לֹא יִשְׁחֲטוּ״ focuses on the animals not being slaughtered, no matter who does it. That alone would include two slaughterers. Since the תורה instead used ״לֹא תִשְׁחֲטוּ״, addressed to the people slaughtering, the wording leaves room for the earlier lesson too.

keyTerms.meaning: They shall not be slaughtered (focused on the animals, not the person)

phrases.english: If so, let it write "they shall not be slaughtered"!
Why does it say "you shall not slaughter" (plural)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that an alternative wording could have taught the point, so the actual wording carries more
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plural is used up by including two slaughterers.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״לֹא יִשְׁחֲטוּ״ would have covered two people, so ״לֹא תִשְׁחֲטוּ״ teaches an extra lesson.

steps.title: Learn two lessons from it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that ״לֹא תִשְׁחֲטוּ״ teaches two things: the איסור applies even with two slaughterers, and the earlier lesson also stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Conclude two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up. The one plural word gives us both lessons, so the earlier דרשה is defended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first lesson is that even two different people are included in the איסור. The second is the earlier lesson that the challenge in step 1 questioned: the reverse order, slaughtering the mother after its child, is also forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it / conclude from it
Two (things)

steps.whatToRemember: ״לֹא תִשְׁחֲטוּ״ teaches two lessons at once. The proof is that the תורה could have used either ״לֹא תִשְׁחוֹט״ or ״לֹא יִשְׁחֲטוּ״ and chose this wording instead.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא method: test a דרשה by asking what other wording the תורה could have used, and learn from the wording it actually chose.

phrases.english: Conclude two things from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from the answer in step 4
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The plural ״לֹא תִשְׁחֲטוּ״ teaches both that two slaughterers are included and the earlier extra lesson.

steps.title: אביי asks for the reason behind סומכוס's eighty lashes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of slaughtering a mother and its granddaughter, and then the daughter. אביי asks רב יוסף why סומכוס gives eighty lashes there.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the משנה's case where someone slaughtered the mother and its granddaughter: אביי asked רב יוסף, what is סומכוס's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the opening words of a case in the משנה. אביי then asks a question, which sets up the two options that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the daughter is connected to two animals that were already slaughtered: its mother and its own daughter. The רבנן give forty lashes and סומכוס gives eighty. אביי wants to know what rule drives סומכוס's double punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: Its daughter's daughter (the granddaughter)
What is the reason?

phrases.english: One slaughtered it and its daughter's daughter,
Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
What is the reason of Sumakhos?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic in the משנה, moving on from the דרשה of לא תשחטו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What rule makes סומכוס give eighty lashes instead of forty?

steps.title: First option: a general rule of double liability
steps.stepSummary: Maybe סומכוס holds a general rule: someone who eats two כזיתים of חלב in one העלם brings two חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does סומכוס hold that someone who ate two olive-sized pieces of forbidden fat in one lapse of awareness must bring two sin offerings?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first possible answer to אביי's question. סומכוס might hold a general rule that breaking the same איסור twice in one go counts as two separate sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most hold that two כזיתים of חלב eaten in one העלם bring only one חטאת. If סומכוס disagrees and counts each כזית on its own, the same logic applies to lashes. One act of slaughter that breaks אותו ואת בנו twice would then earn two sets of lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-sized amount, the minimum amount for punishment
Forbidden fat of an animal
One lapse of awareness, meaning he did not realize in between
A sin offering brought for doing an איסור by mistake

phrases.english: Does Sumakhos hold:
one who ate two olive-bulks of forbidden fat
during one lapse of awareness
is liable to two sin offerings?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the first possible reason for the question in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is סומכוס's reason a general rule that the same איסור done twice gets a double punishment?

steps.title: Why the משנה chose this case if the rule is general
steps.stepSummary: If option one is right, the משנה could have taught the argument in a simple general case. It chose this case to show how far the רבנן go: even with separate animals, they give only one punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה really should have taught this argument in a general case. It taught it here to show the strength of the רבנן's view: even though the two animals are separate bodies, the רבנן still exempt him from a second punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside option one, the גמרא answers a question the learner might ask. If סומכוס's rule is general, why does the משנה bring it in this odd case?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A simple case like eating two pieces of חלב would have taught סומכוס's view. The משנה picked this case because it is the strongest one for the רבנן. Here the daughter is tied to two different animals (גופין מוחלקין), and the רבנן still give only one set of lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: In general, in an ordinary case
To show you the strength or reach of their view
Separate bodies, here two different animals
They exempt

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase "כֹּחָן דְּרַבָּנַן" is about the רבנן, not סומכוס. The משנה chose this case to show how strongly the רבנן hold their view.

phrases.english: And by right it should have taught us in a general case,
and the reason it teaches us in this case
is to let you know the strength of the Rabbis,
that even though the bodies are separate,
the Rabbis exempt him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports option one by explaining why the משנה chose this case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the משנה's choice of case as a way to show the strength of the opposing view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If סומכוס's rule were general, the משנה should have used a simple case like eating two pieces of חלב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה used this case to show that the רבנן exempt even when separate bodies are involved.

steps.title: Second option: separate bodies make the difference
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe סומכוס agrees that two כזיתים of חלב bring only one חטאת. In that case he gives eighty lashes here only because the two other animals are separate bodies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps סומכוס holds that someone who ate two pieces of חלב in one lapse brings only one חטאת, and here the reason for double lashes is that the bodies are separate?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second possible answer. סומכוס's double punishment may be a special rule for this case, not a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this option, doing the same איסור twice normally gives only one punishment, even according to סומכוס. His eighty lashes come from the fact that two different animals each forbid the daughter. That separateness turns one act into two punishments.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps, which introduces the second side of a question
Since, because

phrases.english: Or perhaps Sumakhos holds:

phrases.aramaic: אָכַל שְׁנֵי זֵיתֵי חֵלֶב בְּהֶעְלֵם אֶחָד
phrases.english: one who ate two olive-bulks of forbidden fat during one lapse of awareness
is liable to only one,
and here this is the reason:
since the bodies are separate?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite possibility to option one in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is סומכוס's reason instead special to this case, because the bodies are separate?

steps.title: רב יוסף: סומכוס holds the general rule
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that סומכוס holds the general rule: two כזיתים of חלב in one העלם bring two חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: Yes, סומכוס holds that someone who ate two pieces of חלב in one lapse of awareness brings two חטאות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף picks option one. סומכוס's eighty lashes come from a general rule of double liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying "yes" and repeating the first option shows that סומכוס holds the same rule everywhere. This also confirms the explanation in step 8: the משנה used this case to show that the רבנן exempt even when separate bodies are involved.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יוסף, סומכוס holds a general rule: one act that breaks the same איסור twice gets a double punishment (two חטאות, or two sets of lashes). The משנה brings their argument in the case of separate animals to show how far the רבנן's view reaches.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
phrases.notes: רב יוסף is saying yes to the first option, and he repeats it to make clear which one he means.

phrases.english: he holds that one who ate two olive-bulks of forbidden fat
during one lapse of awareness is liable to two sin offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the question by choosing option one over option two.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סומכוס holds the general rule that two כזיתים of חלב in one העלם bring two חטאות. That is why he gives eighty lashes here.

steps.title: The source: one who sows diverse kinds twice is lashed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רב יוסף's source and quotes a teaching about someone who sows כלאים כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? From what we learned: one who sows כלאים, כלאים, gets lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רב יוסף knows what סומכוס holds. It then brings a teaching about sowing forbidden mixtures as the start of a proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is not finished yet. The next steps will show that this teaching gives two sets of lashes for one act, which would fit סומכוס.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? (asking for a source)
Forbidden mixtures of seeds that may not be planted together
He receives lashes (מלקות)

phrases.english: From where do we know this?
From what we learned:
One who sows diverse kinds, diverse kinds, is lashed.
phrases.notes: He plants two forbidden mixtures, for example wheat with a grape seed and barley with a grape seed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for a source for רב יוסף's answer in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that סומכוס gives two punishments for two כזיתים eaten in one העלם
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching: הזורע כלאים כלאים לוקה

steps.title: What does 'is lashed' mean here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how many lashes are meant. Just one set would be obvious, and it would not explain why the word כלאים is said twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'he is lashed' mean? If you say he gets one set of lashes, that is obvious! And also, why does it say 'כלאים, כלאים'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what 'he is lashed' means. It pushes away the idea that he gets only one set of lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of course someone who sows כלאים gets lashed, so the teaching would not need to say it. Also, if there were only one punishment, the doubled word 'כלאים כלאים' would have no purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious (so why would the text need to teach it?)
And furthermore (adding a second argument)

phrases.english: What does 'is lashed' mean?
If you say he is lashed once, that is obvious!
And furthermore, why say 'diverse kinds, diverse kinds'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the wording of the teaching quoted in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How many sets of lashes the sower of כלאים כלאים receives.

steps.title: He gets two sets of lashes
steps.stepSummary: Since one set would be obvious, the teaching must mean two sets of lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that he gets two sets of lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the teaching means two sets of lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the first piece of the proof: the sower of two mixtures is punished twice. Next the גמרא must figure out in what kind of case this happened.

keyTerms.meaning: Two sets of lashes

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that it means two sets of lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The teaching means two sets of lashes.

steps.title: Was it two separate acts with two warnings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case this is. It cannot be two separate acts with two warnings, because the משנה about the נזיר already teaches that.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If you say he sowed one after the other, with two warnings, we already learned that: a נזיר who drank wine all day is liable only once. If they told him 'Don't drink!' and he drank, 'Don't drink!' and he drank, he is liable for each one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case the teaching is talking about. It rules out a case of two separate acts with two warnings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה of the נזיר already teaches that each new warning followed by a new act brings a new punishment. So a teaching about כלאים would add nothing if it meant that case.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
A warning given before a sin. It is needed before lashes can be given.
One after the other (at separate times)
A person who took a vow not to drink wine, among other things

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with?
If you say it was one after the other
and with two warnings,
we already learned this:

phrases.aramaic: נָזִיר שֶׁהָיָה שׁוֹתֶה יַיִן כׇּל הַיּוֹם
phrases.english: A נזיר who was drinking wine all day
is liable only once;
if they told him 'Don't drink!' and he drinks,
'Don't drink!' and he drinks,
he is liable for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִילֵימָא בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה וּבִשְׁתֵּי הַתְרָאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that we know it means two sets of lashes, asks what kind of case gives them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the two acts of sowing were separate with separate warnings, or at once with one warning.

steps.title: It was at the same time with one warning
steps.stepSummary: The case must be two acts of sowing done at once, after only one warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that he did it at one time, with one warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the teaching is about sowing both mixtures at the same moment after a single warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the teaching says something new: one action with one warning brings two sets of lashes. This is just like סומכוס's view that one act can bring two punishments.

keyTerms.meaning: At one time, together
A single warning

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that it was at one time
and with one warning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא בְּבַת אַחַת וּבְהַתְרָאָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 14 by choosing the other kind of case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two acts of sowing at once, with one warning, bring two sets of lashes.

steps.title: Whose view is this? Not the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who taught this. It cannot be the רבנן: they give only one punishment even for separate animals, so surely only one for seeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say it is the רבנן who argue with סומכוס, then: if there, where the animals are separate bodies, the רבנן give only one punishment, here, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the teaching follows. It argues that it cannot be the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the רבנן give only one set of lashes even though the animals are separate bodies. Seeds sown together are not separate bodies like animals, so by a כל שכן the רבנן would surely give only one set of lashes here.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
Separate bodies (here, separate animals)
All the more so
They exempt (here, from a second punishment)

phrases.english: Whose view is this?
If you say it is the Rabbis who disagree with סומכוס,
now, if there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the משנה's case: the mother and granddaughter, then the daughter (Step 6).

phrases.english: where the bodies are separate, the Rabbis exempt him,
here, is it not all the more so?
phrases.notes: Seeds planted together are not separate bodies the way animals are.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי? אִילֵּימָא רַבָּנַן דִּפְלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּסוֹמְכוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the case from Step 15 to figure out whose view the teaching follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא the teaching follows; the רבנן seem ruled out by a כל שכן.

steps.title: So it must follow סומכוס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the teaching follows סומכוס, which would prove רב יוסף's claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not סומכוס?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof: the teaching must be סומכוס's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching gives two punishments for one act with one warning, even without separate bodies. If this is סומכוס, then he gives two punishments even where the bodies are not separate, like two כזיתים of חלב. That is exactly what רב יוסף said.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not...? (offering the likely conclusion)

phrases.english: Rather, is it not סומכוס?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion after the רבנן were ruled out in Step 16.
steps.raayaObject: סומכוס holds that two כזיתים of חלב in one העלם bring two חטאות
steps.raayaSupportSource: The כלאים teaching, read as following סומכוס

steps.title: No: it can follow the רבנן, and teaches two kinds of כלאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The teaching follows the רבנן, and the doubled word only teaches in passing that there are two kinds of כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it really is the רבנן. It teaches us something in passing: there are two kinds of כלאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof and says the teaching can follow the רבנן after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof ruled out a case of two separate acts with two warnings, because the נזיר משנה already teaches that. The גמרא now says the case can be exactly that: two separate acts, each with its own warning, which fits the רבנן. It is not a repeat of the נזיר משנה, because the doubled 'כלאים כלאים' adds a side lesson: there are two different kinds of כלאים. So the teaching does not have to follow סומכוס, and it does not prove רב יוסף's claim.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (keeping the first option)
In passing, on the way
It teaches us
Two kinds, two types

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the רבנן now agree with סומכוס. The גמרא only removes the proof: the doubled word is explained another way.
steps.whatToRemember: The כלאים teaching could have proven רב יוסף's view of סומכוס. It was rejected because the doubled word 'כלאים כלאים' can be teaching that there are two kinds of כלאים.

phrases.english: No, it really is the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִילְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
phrases.english: and it teaches us something in passing:
that there are two kinds of diverse kinds.
phrases.notes: For example, wheat with a grape seed is one kind, and barley with a grape seed is another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in Step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the כלאים teaching must follow סומכוס, so it no longer proves רב יוסף's claim.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed a case of separate acts with two warnings would add nothing beyond the נזיר משנה. In fact it adds the lesson that there are two kinds of כלאים, so the ברייתא can be about two warnings and follow the רבנן.

steps.title: The extra teaching argues with רבי יאשיה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא about two kinds of כלאים is needed to reject רבי יאשיה, who says a person is only liable when he sows wheat, barley and grape seed together in one throw.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא also comes to reject the view of רבי יאשיה. רבי יאשיה says a person is not liable until he sows wheat, barley and a grape seed in one throw of the hand. The ברייתא teaches that even if he sows only wheat with a grape seed, or only barley with a grape seed, he is also liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the ברייתא is really teaching, now that it is read as following the רבנן. Its point is to argue with רבי יאשיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה needs two kinds of seed plus a grape seed together before there is liability. The ברייתא teaches that one kind of seed with a grape seed is already enough. So the ברייתא says nothing about two punishments for one act, and the proof for סומכוס is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, meaning to reject a certain opinion
A single throw of the hand when sowing
A grape seed
The ban on planting other seeds together with grapes in a vineyard

steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to prove סומכוס's view from כלאים failed. The ברייתא is only arguing with רבי יאשיה about how many kinds of seed are needed.

phrases.english: And it comes to exclude the view of רבי יאשיה,
as רבי יאשיה says:
He is not liable until he sows wheat, barley and a grape seed
with one throw of the hand.
So it teaches us
that when he sows wheat and a grape seed
or barley and a grape seed,
he is also liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the rejection in step 18 by saying what the ברייתא is really teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the teaching a different purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The doubled wording seemed to teach two punishments, which would follow סומכוס.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that wheat or barley with a grape seed is already forbidden, against רבי יאשיה.

steps.title: A new source: eating from both גיד הנשה nerves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: someone who eats an olive-size from each גיד הנשה gets eighty lashes, while רבי יהודה says only forty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If someone ate an olive-size from this nerve and an olive-size from that nerve, he gets eighty lashes. רבי יהודה says he gets only forty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attempt to answer the question about two punishments for one act. It quotes a משנה and will explain the case in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two גיד הנשה nerves, one in each back leg. The תנא קמא gives two sets of forty lashes and רבי יהודה gives one. The גמרא now needs to work out what case the משנה is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: The sciatic nerve, which the Torah forbids eating
An olive-size, the amount that makes one liable
Receives (lashes)
Eighty, meaning two sets of forty lashes

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If one ate an olive-size from this one and an olive-size from that one,
phrases.notes: This is the גיד הנשה of the right leg and the one of the left leg of the same animal.

phrases.english: he receives eighty lashes.
רבי יהודה says:
He receives only forty.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אָכַל מִזֶּה כְּזַיִת וּמִזֶּה כְּזַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the כלאים proof failed, a new source is brought for the same question.
steps.raayaObject: Whether one act after one warning can bring two sets of lashes
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about eating from both גיד הנשה nerves

steps.title: It cannot be two separate acts with two warnings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the case is. If he ate one after the other with two warnings, רבי יהודה should give no lashes at all, because he holds an uncertain warning does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say he ate them one after the other, with two warnings, what would רבי יהודה's reason be? Each warning is an uncertain warning, and we know that רבי יהודה says an uncertain warning is not a real warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to define the case of the משנה. It rules out the case of two separate acts with two warnings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, only one of the two nerves is really forbidden, but we don't know which. So each separate warning might be about the permitted nerve. Since he holds such a warning does not count, he would give no lashes at all, not forty.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the details?
A warning given before a sin, needed for lashes
An uncertain warning, where it is not clear the act is really forbidden

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say one after the other
and with two warnings,
what is רבי יהודה's reason for forty?
It is an uncertain warning,
phrases.notes: For רבי יהודה only one leg's nerve is forbidden, and we don't know which, so each warning may be about the wrong one.

phrases.english: and we have heard that רבי יהודה says:
An uncertain warning is not called a warning.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה וּבִשְׁתֵּי הַתְרָאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts defining the case of the משנה quoted in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Exactly how the person ate the two nerves: separately or together, with how many warnings.

steps.title: Proof: רבי יהודה and the man unsure who his father is
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה's view: if someone unsure which of two men is his father hits them one after the other, he is exempt; if he hits both at once, he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: If he hit this one and then hit that one, or cursed this one and then cursed that one, or hit both at once, or cursed both at once, he is liable. רבי יהודה says: at once, he is liable; one after the other, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove what it just said about רבי יהודה, that an uncertain warning does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he hits the men one at a time, each warning is uncertain, since this man may not be his father, so רבי יהודה exempts him. When he hits both at once, one of them is surely his father, so the warning is certain and he is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: At the same time, in one act
One after the other
Hit (a father, a capital sin)
Cursed (a father, a capital sin)
Exempt, not punished

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: הִכָּה אֶת זֶה וְחָזַר וְהִכָּה אֶת זֶה,
phrases.english: If he hit this one and then hit that one,
phrases.notes: The case is someone who doesn't know which of two men is his father.

phrases.aramaic: קִלֵּל אֶת זֶה וְחָזַר וְקִלֵּל אֶת זֶה,
phrases.english: or cursed this one and then cursed that one,
or hit both of them at once,
or cursed both of them at once,
he is liable.
רבי יהודה says:
At once, he is liable;
one after the other, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הִכָּה אֶת זֶה וְחָזַר וְהִכָּה אֶת זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 21 that רבי יהודה rejects an uncertain warning.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה holds that an uncertain warning is not a valid warning
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about hitting or cursing two men when one is surely the father

steps.title: The case is eating both at once with one warning
steps.stepSummary: Since separate acts would bring no lashes for רבי יהודה, the משנה must be talking about eating both nerves at once after one warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that the case is where he ate both at once, with one warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes what the case of the משנה must be: one act of eating both nerves, after a single warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating both together means he surely ate the forbidden nerve, so רבי יהודה gives forty. This sets up the next point: the תנא קמא gives eighty even for one act with one warning.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
A single warning

steps.whyThisMatters: This is exactly the case that matters for רב יוסף's claim about סומכוס: one act, one warning. Now the גמרא can see what the משנה rules in that case.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that it is
at once and with one warning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא בְּבַת אַחַת וּבְהַתְרָאָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21 after ruling out separate acts.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה is about eating both nerves at the same time after one warning.

steps.title: The first opinion in the משנה must be סומכוס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the תנא קמא is. It cannot be the רבנן, because they give only one set of lashes for one warning even when the bodies are separate. So it must be סומכוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the first תנא? If you say it is the רבנן who argue with סומכוס, there is a problem. There, where the bodies are separate, the רבנן exempt him. Here it should be all the more so! So isn't it סומכוס?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the first opinion in the גיד הנשה משנה, the one giving eighty lashes. It concludes that it must be סומכוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה of אותו ואת בנו, the רבנן give only one set of lashes for one warning, even though the animals are separate bodies. Two nerves are less separate than that, so the רבנן would surely exempt him here too. Only סומכוס, who gives lashes for each act even after one warning, could give eighty.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא
If you say (it is suggested, then rejected)
Separate bodies, meaning distinct physical items
All the more so

phrases.english: And who is the first tanna?
phrases.notes: This is the first opinion in the גיד הנשה משנה, the one that gives eighty lashes.

phrases.english: If you say it is the Rabbis who argue with Sumakhos,
phrases.notes: This refers to their argument in the משנה about אותו ואת בנו.

phrases.english: now, if there,
where the bodies are separate, the Rabbis exempt him,
here, is it not all the more so?
Rather, is it not Sumakhos?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן תַּנָּא קַמָּא? אִילֵימָא רַבָּנַן דִּפְלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּסוֹמְכוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that the משנה is about eating both at once with one warning, and identifies who could hold that view.
steps.raayaObject: That the first opinion in the גיד הנשה משנה follows סומכוס
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the רבנן's ruling in אותו ואת בנו, where they exempt even for separate bodies

steps.title: No: one after the other, following the רבנן and another view of רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה can be about eating the nerves one after the other, following the רבנן. The problem about רבי יהודה goes away if this תנא has a different tradition about his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really it is talking about one after the other, and it follows the רבנן. And this תנא holds like the other תנא's version of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the claim that the משנה follows סומכוס. It says the case can be two separate acts with two warnings, following the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21's difficulty was that, for רבי יהודה, an uncertain warning does not count, so separate acts would get no lashes. The גמרא answers that there is another תנא who reports רבי יהודה differently. In that report, an uncertain warning does count, so forty lashes makes sense even for separate acts.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (going back to the original reading)
One after the other, as separate acts
The other תנא, a different tradition

steps.confusionAlert: The disagreement here is not about what רבי יהודה thinks in general. It is about two different reports of his opinion, passed down by two different תנאים.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, לְעוֹלָם בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה, וְרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: No, actually it is one after the other, and it is the Rabbis,
and this tanna holds it
phrases.notes: This is the תנא who reports רבי יהודה's forty lashes in our משנה.

phrases.english: like the other tanna's version of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 24 by offering a different case and a different tradition of רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the conclusion that the משנה must follow סומכוס
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed רבי יהודה says התראת ספק does not count. Another tradition says it does, so the משנה can be about separate acts with two warnings.

steps.title: Source for the view that התראת ספק counts: the נותר of the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: The other תנא holds that, for רבי יהודה, התראת ספק counts as a warning. The גמרא begins a ברייתא on the פסוק about not leaving over the קרבן פסח until morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: He says an uncertain warning is a real warning, as it is taught in a ברייתא: 'Do not leave any of it until morning, and what is left of it until morning, burn in fire.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the other tradition: for רבי יהודה, התראת ספק counts as a warning. It then starts quoting a ברייתא to show where this view appears, and the explanation continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up the proof for the alternative tradition of רבי יהודה. The ברייתא opens with the פסוק about נותר, the leftover meat of the קרבן פסח. Its analysis will show how a warning can count even when it is not certain that a punishable sin will happen.

keyTerms.meaning: An uncertain warning, given when it is unclear whether the act will end up being punishable
It is considered a warning
Leftover sacrificial meat that must be burned
You shall not leave over

phrases.english: For he says: an uncertain warning is considered a warning,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the other תנא, reporting רבי יהודה's view.

phrases.english: as it is taught: 'You shall not leave any of it until morning,'

phrases.aramaic: וְהַנֹּתָר מִמֶּנּוּ עַד בֹּקֶר בָּאֵשׁ תִּשְׂרֹפוּ״ –
phrases.english: 'and what remains of it until morning you shall burn in fire.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר: הַתְרָאַת סָפֵק שְׁמָהּ הַתְרָאָה, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the other tradition of רבי יהודה that Step 25 relied on.
steps.raayaObject: That according to one tradition, רבי יהודה holds התראת ספק counts as a warning
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on the פסוק of נותר of the קרבן פסח (שמות 12:10), which continues past this point
